A Client resource describes a File Daemon the Director backs up: where to reach it, how to authenticate, and limits and quotas for its jobs.

## Examples

**A typical Linux client**

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Address = web.example.com
  Password = "client-secret"
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 2
}
```

**A client behind NAT that connects to the Director**

```text
Client {
  Name = laptop-fd
  Address = laptop.example.com
  Password = "laptop-secret"
  Connection From Director To Client = no
  Connection From Client To Director = yes
}
```

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name · Required

Name of the client as jobs, the catalog and the job logs know it. Renaming it starts a new history in the catalog, since jobs are stored by client.

```text
Client {
  Name = "web-fd"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add client name=web-fd address=web.example.com password=client-secret
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the client.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Description = "Web server"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd description="Web server"
```

### Protocol {#d-protocol}

Key: `protocol` · Type: enum · Default: `Native` · Values: `Native`, `NDMPv2`, `NDMPv3`, `NDMPv4`

Protocol to talk to the client: Native (the Bareos File Daemon) or one of the NDMP versions for NAS filers.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Protocol = Native
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd protocol=Native
```

### Auth Type {#d-authtype}

Key: `authtype` · Type: enum · Default: `None` · Values: `None`, `Clear`, `MD5`

Authentication for NDMP clients: None, Clear or MD5. Native clients ignore it.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Auth Type = MD5
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd authtype=MD5
```

### Address {#d-address}

Key: `address` · Type: string · Aliases: FD Address · Required

Host name or IP address of the File Daemon. Required, since the Director connects to it (unless Connection From Client To Director is used).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Address = "web.example.com"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd address=web.example.com
```

### Lan Address {#d-lanaddress}

Key: `lanaddress` · Type: string

Address used instead of Address when the Storage Daemon connects to the File Daemon in passive mode, for setups where storage and client share a LAN that the Director does not see.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Lan Address = "10.0.0.21"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd lanaddress=10.0.0.21
```

Key: `port` · Type: positive integer · Default: `9102` · Aliases: FD Port

TCP port of the File Daemon.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Port = 9102
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd port=9102
```

Key: `password` · Type: password · Aliases: FD Password · Required

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Password = "client-secret"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd password=client-secret
```

Key: `catalog` · Type: resource

Catalog the jobs of this client are stored in, for installations with several catalogs.

```text
  Name = web-fd
  Catalog = "MyCatalog"
```

### Passive {#d-passive}

Key: `passive` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Passive mode: the Storage Daemon connects to the File Daemon instead of the other way round. Useful when the client may not open connections, for example behind a firewall.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Passive = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd passive=yes
```

### Connection From Director To Client {#d-connectionfromdirectortoclient}

Key: `connectionfromdirectortoclient` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

The Director opens the connection to the File Daemon (the normal case).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Connection From Director To Client = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd connectionfromdirectortoclient=yes
```

### Connection From Client To Director {#d-connectionfromclienttodirector}

Key: `connectionfromclienttodirector` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

The File Daemon connects to the Director and keeps the connection open, so a client behind NAT or a firewall can be backed up. Needs the matching setting in the File Daemon. With Run On Incoming Connect Interval a job can start when the client connects.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Connection From Client To Director = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd connectionfromclienttodirector=yes
```

### Enabled {#d-enabled}

Key: `enabled` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

A disabled client is not backed up by scheduled jobs; enable client and disable client change it at run time.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Enabled = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd enabled=yes
```

### Hard Quota {#d-hardquota}

Key: `hardquota` · Type: size · Default: `0`

Upper limit for the data of this client; a backup that would go beyond it fails. 0 means no limit. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Hard Quota = 500 g
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd hardquota="500 g"
```

### Soft Quota {#d-softquota}

Key: `softquota` · Type: size · Default: `0`

Soft limit for the data of this client: beyond it a warning is written, and after the Soft Quota Grace Period jobs fail. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Soft Quota = 400 g
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd softquota="400 g"
```

### Soft Quota Grace Period {#d-softquotagraceperiod}

Key: `softquotagraceperiod` · Type: time · Default: `0`

How long the soft quota may be exceeded before jobs fail. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Soft Quota Grace Period = 7 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd softquotagraceperiod="7 days"
```

### Strict Quotas {#d-strictquotas}

Key: `strictquotas` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

When the soft quota grace period has run out: yes makes the soft quota a hard limit; no lets jobs run up to the hard quota.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Strict Quotas = no
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd strictquotas=no
```

### Quota Include Failed Jobs {#d-quotaincludefailedjobs}

Key: `quotaincludefailedjobs` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Count the data of failed jobs into the quota.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Quota Include Failed Jobs = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd quotaincludefailedjobs=yes
```

### File Retention {#d-fileretention}

Key: `fileretention` · Type: time · Default: `5184000` (2 months) · Deprecated

Deprecated in Bareos 25: how long file records of this client's jobs are kept. Set retention in the Pool instead. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  File Retention = 60 days
}
```

### Job Retention {#d-jobretention}

Key: `jobretention` · Type: time · Default: `15552000` (6 months) · Deprecated

Deprecated in Bareos 25: how long job records of this client are kept. Set retention in the Pool instead. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Job Retention = 6 months
}
```

### Heartbeat Interval {#d-heartbeatinterval}

Key: `heartbeatinterval` · Type: time · Default: `0`

Interval of keep-alive packets to the File Daemon. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Heartbeat Interval = 60
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd heartbeatinterval=60
```

### Auto Prune {#d-autoprune}

Key: `autoprune` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no` · Deprecated

Deprecated in Bareos 25: prune this client's jobs and files after each job.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Auto Prune = no
}
```

### Maximum Concurrent Jobs {#d-maximumconcurrentjobs}

Key: `maximumconcurrentjobs` · Type: positive integer · Default: `1`

How many jobs may run on this client at the same time; further jobs wait. Raise it when several jobs (for example per file system) back up the same host.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 2
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd maximumconcurrentjobs=2
```

### Maximum Bandwidth Per Job {#d-maximumbandwidthperjob}

Key: `maximumbandwidthperjob` · Type: speed

Limits the bandwidth of each job of this client. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  Maximum Bandwidth Per Job = 20 m/s
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd maximumbandwidthperjob="20 m/s"
```

### NDMP Log Level {#d-ndmploglevel}

Key: `ndmploglevel` · Type: positive integer · Default: `4`

Detail of NDMP messages of this client, 0 to 9.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  NDMP Log Level = 4
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd ndmploglevel=4
```

### NDMP Block Size {#d-ndmpblocksize}

Key: `ndmpblocksize` · Type: size · Default: `64512`

Block size of NDMP backups. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  NDMP Block Size = 64512
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd ndmpblocksize=64512
```

### NDMP Use LMDB {#d-ndmpuselmdb}

Key: `ndmpuselmdb` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Keep the NDMP file history in an LMDB database during the job instead of in memory, for filers with many files.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  NDMP Use LMDB = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd ndmpuselmdb=yes
```

### TLS Authenticate {#d-tlsauthenticate}

Key: `tlsauthenticate` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Use TLS only to authenticate the peer and switch back to an unencrypted connection afterwards. The data then travels in clear text, so this is meant for networks that are protected otherwise. Bareos' default TLS-PSK setup does not need it.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Authenticate = no
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsauthenticate=no
```

### TLS Enable {#d-tlsenable}

Key: `tlsenable` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Enable TLS for this connection. Since Bareos 18.2 TLS is on by default and uses TLS-PSK with the password of the resource, so no certificates are needed; set it to no only for peers that cannot speak TLS.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Enable = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsenable=yes
```

### TLS Require {#d-tlsrequire}

Key: `tlsrequire` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Refuse connections that do not use TLS. With the default (yes) a peer without TLS cannot connect; set it to no only during a migration from very old clients.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Require = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsrequire=yes
```

### TLS Cipher List {#d-tlscipherlist}

Key: `tlscipherlist` · Type: string

OpenSSL cipher list for TLS 1.2 and older, colon separated. Leave it empty to use the OpenSSL defaults; restrict it only when a security policy demands specific ciphers.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Cipher List = "PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384:PSK-AES128-GCM-SHA256"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlscipherlist=PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384:PSK-AES128-GCM-SHA256
```

### TLS Cipher Suites {#d-tlsciphersuites}

Key: `tlsciphersuites` · Type: string

OpenSSL cipher suites for TLS 1.3, colon separated. Empty means the OpenSSL defaults.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Cipher Suites = "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsciphersuites=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384:TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
```

### TLS DH File {#d-tlsdhfile}

Key: `tlsdhfile` · Type: path

PEM file with Diffie-Hellman parameters for the DH key exchange of TLS 1.2. Without it, ephemeral DH ciphers are not offered; ECDHE and PSK ciphers do not need it.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS DH File = "/etc/bareos/tls/dh2048.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsdhfile=/etc/bareos/tls/dh2048.pem
```

### TLS Protocol {#d-tlsprotocol}

Key: `tlsprotocol` · Type: string

Restricts the TLS protocol versions in OpenSSL syntax, for example to forbid old versions. Empty means the OpenSSL default.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Protocol = "-ALL, +TLSv1.2, +TLSv1.3"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsprotocol="-ALL, +TLSv1.2, +TLSv1.3"
```

### TLS Verify Peer {#d-tlsverifypeer}

Key: `tlsverifypeer` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

With certificate based TLS: check the peer's certificate against the CA and, for a server, against TLS Allowed CN. It has no effect with TLS-PSK.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Verify Peer = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsverifypeer=yes
```

### TLS Ca Certificate File {#d-tlscacertificatefile}

Key: `tlscacertificatefile` · Type: path

PEM file with the CA certificates used to verify the peer's certificate. Needed for certificate based TLS when TLS Verify Peer is on (or use TLS CA Certificate Dir).

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Ca Certificate File = "/etc/bareos/tls/ca.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlscacertificatefile=/etc/bareos/tls/ca.pem
```

### TLS Ca Certificate Dir {#d-tlscacertificatedir}

Key: `tlscacertificatedir` · Type: path

Directory of hashed CA certificates (as made by openssl rehash), an alternative to TLS CA Certificate File.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Ca Certificate Dir = "/etc/ssl/certs"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlscacertificatedir=/etc/ssl/certs
```

### TLS Certificate Revocation List {#d-tlscertificaterevocationlist}

Key: `tlscertificaterevocationlist` · Type: path

PEM file with a certificate revocation list; certificates on it are refused.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Certificate Revocation List = "/etc/bareos/tls/crl.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlscertificaterevocationlist=/etc/bareos/tls/crl.pem
```

### TLS Certificate {#d-tlscertificate}

Key: `tlscertificate` · Type: path

PEM file with the own certificate for certificate based TLS. Goes together with TLS Key.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Certificate = "/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.pem"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlscertificate=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.pem
```

### TLS Key {#d-tlskey}

Key: `tlskey` · Type: path

PEM file with the private key of TLS Certificate. Keep it readable for the daemon user only.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Key = "/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.key"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlskey=/etc/bareos/tls/bareos-dir.key
```

### TLS Allowed CN {#d-tlsallowedcn}

Key: `tlsallowedcn` · Type: string list

Common names a peer certificate may carry; others are refused when TLS Verify Peer is on. Repeat the directive for several names.

```text
Client {
  Name = web-fd
  TLS Allowed CN = "client1.example.com"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update client=web-fd tlsallowedcn=client1.example.com
```
